[roadway]. u1 exited the driveway of [roadway] and turned right to go south on [roadway]. both driver and passenger observed a male in the middle of the roadway approximately 75 yards south of their complete stop straddling the right and left lanes, waiting [roadway]. both the driver and passenger observed the male turn to look at them and then suddenly started running towards their vehicle. driver of u1 panicked and hit the accelerator and tried to swerve to avoid the pedestrian, but hit the pedestrian instead. the male was struck on the front passenger side. he rolled up onto [roadway] and struck the windshield on the passenger side, causing damage. the male was thrown off the vehicle and landed in the roadway. once driver of u1 saw the male stand up to walk away, he drove away and the passenger called 911. the pedestrian initially refused to give any information and insisted he didn't want a report. he had quite a bit of injury, [roadway] rash on his arms and back, but refused medical treatment. he did eventually provide some necessary information for the report, but would not say where he was coming from or his exact location when the accident occurred. he said he ran across the roadway and was hit. he also said his children had been with him, but were already on the sidewalk and had not been injured. he refused to give his address and would not allow officers to converse with his children. driver and passenger of u1 advised it was only him in the roadway and no children or other persons were [roadway]. pedestrian did not appear to be intoxicated nor suicidal. he was simply uncooperative. given the lack of cooperation from the pedestrian, no charges were filed in this case (per ai ritcheson and sgt. blank). both u1 and the pedestrian were shown to have possibly caused the accident. the driver of u1 admitted to panicking and trying to swerve around the pedestrian. the pedestrian possibly failed to yield the right of way to the vehicle. driver of u1 was cited for fmfr. u1 was not towed because it was already parked at a residence quite a distance away from the accident location.

records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 was traveling westbound on ih 30 approaching the 214 mile post. driver of non contact unit 1 & 2 were parked on the improved shoulder in a no parking zone on the ih 30 [roadway]. both drivers were outside their units and standing on the improved shoulder near non contact unit 2. unit 1 exited ih 30 at the 213 exit ramp and crossed over the white fog line. unit 1 struck both pedestrians causing serious bodily injury. unit 1 failed to stop and render aid and fled the scene. the only evidence left from unit 1 on scene was a portion of the passenger side mirror. both pedestrians stated that the car that struck them was a white toyota camry, but could not provide any additional information. the driver of the non contact unit 2 advised me that his truck tractor was equipped with a dash camera. i later reviewed the video recording of the incident and was able to get a license plate number off of unit 1. the license plate returned to a white 2004 toyota camry registered to america's car-mart. i later made contact with the car-mart assistant manager who informed me that unit 1 was in their rear parking lot. i observed unit 1 on scene with corresponding damage to the crash and the documented license plate from the video. the assistant manager contacted me on the following day and informed me that the suspect was in car-mart's office lobby. i arrived and interviewed the suspect, driver of unit 1. driver of unit 1 stated he was operating at the time of the crash and also admitted to taking sleep prior to the crash but had no recollection of hitting pedestrians. i believe beyond a reasonable doubt that glenn hoke garcia was operating unit 1 at the time of the crash.

records.deidentified_narrative: unit 1 was in the north east parking lot of vista verde apartments. to exit the apartment complex, unit 1 made a right turn and began traveling south east. unit 1 made the turn around the corner and struck unit 2. the boyfriend of unit 2 stopped unit 1 and told him he hit his girlfriend, at which time unit 1 fled the scene of the crash without leaving any required information or to see if unit 2 needed medical assistance. the boyfriend described the suspect vehicle as a red f-150 with carpet rolls in the back, but video of unit 1 leaving the property shows a late 90's to early 2000 gray chevrolet pickup truck with a white camper on the back and ladders on top. officer rodriguez identified the point where unit 1 impacted unit 2 by locating the scuff mark of the shoe that unit 2 was wearing, the point where unit 2 struck the ground and the final resting point of unit 2 on the ground (pool of blood from the head). from the scuff mark to where unit 2 struck the ground is approximately 5 feet 1 inch. from where unit 2 struck the [roadway] is approximately 7 feet 4 inches. from the scuff mark to the pool of blood is approximately 11 feet 10 inches. investigation is ongoing.

records.public_safe_text: while assigned to south patrol police responded to the listed location for a report of a major accident. i arrived on location and contacted driver of unit 1 and driver of unit 2 who were still in the roadway. driver of unit 2 advised he was not injured but was very shaken up and requested ems to make the location to check his vital signs. i observed that the steering knob of unit 2 was broken. this rendered the wheelchair immobile. i assisted in pushing unit 2 onto the sidewalk while we waited for ems. witness on scene informed me that unit 2 had a [roadway] and was using the [roadway] legally when unit 1 who was headed south on zarzamora made a right [roadway] and did not see unit 2 until after contact was made. witness on scene advised driver of unit 1 to stop and he stopped and waited for police to arrive. driver of unit 1 stated he looked left to ensure no oncoming traffic was coming and did not see unit 2 prior to making contact at low speed with him. ems cleared driver of unit 2 medically. driver of unit 1 had his mother deliver an extra manual wheelchair to the location. i assisted driver of unit 2 into the wheelchair provided by driver of unit 1. i provided sapd form 12-dar to driver of unit 2 and a sapd form cic-01 to driver of unit 1 and released them both on scene without incident. this is a summary of events. for full details refer to body worn camera and coban video.

records.public_safe_text: with windows down, unit 1 stated to be driving approximately 4 mph through parking lot crowded with people (i. e. unsponsored event / ""car club meeting""). unit 2 stated she saw unit 1 coming as she was standing with a group in front of parked trucks (trucks parked in painted stalls, unit 2 standing in navigatable aisle of parking lot). unit 1 driver and passenger stated they never saw anyone in front of unit 1 and drove passed group of people. shortly after, unit 1 driver and passenger started getting hit with beers being thrown into unit 1 by unknown persons. some of these unknown persons contacted police, claiming unit 1 driver smelt of alcoholic beverages. unit 1 stated they were told they hit unit 2. unit 1 demonstrated her actions after receiving this information to me. unit 1 demonstrated herself, using a patrol vehicle, exiting the driver's door and walking along driver's side to unit 2 who was surrounded by a group. unit 1 driver and passenger couldn't say how unit 2 was struck by unit 1. unit 2 stated she was struck by unit 1 front passenger side tire. unit 2 was unable to state how she initially ended up on the ground. witness stated unit 2 was seen with a group as unit 1 approached slowly. the group moved away from navigatable aisle as unit 1 approached but unit 2 was stated to have been seen moving opposite of group, towards unit 1. unit 2 stated she didn't do this nor did she hear people yelling [roadway] of unit 1 as witness stated. with only one witness identified as seeing the incident start to finish and conflicting stories from unit 1 occupants and unit 2, it's unknown exactly how unit 2 and unit 1 made contact.-eor-

records.public_safe_text: on [date] at approximately 1540 hours, i, officer j. hancock, while working uniformed patrol in a marked patrol vehicle, was dispatched to a vehicle vs pedestrian accident in the walmart parking lot, located at [roadway] 336 west. upon arrival, i observed a green 2003 ford expedition (unit 1), bearing texas license plate [identifier], stopped in front of the grocery side entrance to walmart. i was advised that a black female standing in front of the vehicle was the pedestrian that was struck. i contacted the pedestrian, linda taylor (unit 2), and asked if she was ok. i did not see any obvious injuries as linda leaned on a shopping cart. linda said she had hip surgery in the past and her right hip was hurting where the vehicle struck her. linda said the vehicle struck her with the front left headlight. linda requested medical attention and i was advised by walmart staff that an ambulance was en-route. i asked linda what happened and she said she was walking from the parking lot toward the entrance of walmart across the crosswalk. the driver of the green expedition was looking to the right, away from her, and not paying attention as he blared music. linda said the expedition suddenly sped up and struck her. linda said she did not fall down as a result. i asked linda if she wanted to wait inside, out of the heat, and she said yes. i observed linda walk into the walmart lobby while leaning on the shopping cart, without any obvious limp. i contacted the driver of the ford expedition, elionzo alegria, and asked if he was ok. elionzo said he was ok. i asked elionzo what happened and he told me the following. elionzo was following a vehicle ahead of him, driving slowly across the grocery side entrance crosswalk, which is on the private walmart parking lot. suddenly a black female ran into the front left side of his vehicle as if it was intentional. i asked elionzo if the black female fell after striking his vehicle and he said no. i asked elionzo if there was any damage to his vehicle as a result and he said no. i checked the front of the vehicle and did not observe any damage. i viewed surveillance video from walmart and observed elionzo driving north in his expedition across the grocery side entrance. the expedition was closely following another vehicle, both driving very slowly, so that no reasonable person would try to cross between them. there were several people on the right side of the expedition who were waiting for the vehicles to pass. suddenly, i saw linda approach from the parking lot walking toward walmart. i observed linda walk up to the front left side of the expedition and walk into the headlight area as the expedition came to a stop. it appeared that linda intentionally leaned into the vehicle as it stopped, to strike the vehicle. linda did not fall as a result and the impact appeared to be [roadway] of safety and proceeded into the path of the expedition so close that it was impossible for the expedition operator to yield. linda was transported to hca conroe by medic 14. i provided elionzo [medical facility]. i contacted linda and provided her with a case card to reference the crash report, which was completed due to her claim of injury. linda was at fault for failing to yield to a vehicle, but was not issued a citation [roadway] withing a private parking lot. i received a copy of the walmart surveillance video of this incident and later submitted it into evidence. pedestrian at fault

records.deidentified_narrative: on [date] police responded to pop's chicken reference to a vehicle verses pedestrian accident in the parking lot. upon arrival officer located unit 1 and its driver who was attending to pedestrian who was sitting in a small suv. unit 1 driver stated that she may have backed into the pedestrian, but unit 1 driver was not sure. unit 1 driver stated that none of the sensors went off nor did she see pedestrian in the back up camera. pedestrian complained of discomfort and pain in her left upper arm and left hip. pedestrian also stated that she had previous injuries from an accident 17 years ago on her right side. officer had ems respond. ems checked pedestrian who refused to be transported. officer looked at pedestrians left upper arm as well as her left calf and did not see any marks, scratches or swelling. officer took several photographs of upper arm and calf area that pedestrian stated was injured. officer took several photographs of unit one as well, no damage was visible. officer contacted a witness bill (903) 565-9078 who stated that unit 1 did not strike the pedestrian. bill stated that he was helping carry out lunches along with the pedestrian. officer also spoke with a witness for pedestrian several days later by telephone who stated that she saw the incident and states that unit 1 did strike pedestrian. witness 2 kerri eckenrod works with pedestrian for the champagne group homes in lindale, tx.
